results.title: Add one paragraph after a named paragraph of a rich text

paragraphs: A headless CMS separates the content from the page that shows it. Content managers write once, and every channel reads the same entry.
Planning the content model
Start with the questions your content managers ask every day. A content model that mirrors those questions needs less training.
Read the Payload documentation for the field types, then sketch the model on paper.
Review before publishing
Drafts protect the live site. Content managers save a draft, a second person reads it, and only then it goes live.
A checklist keeps the second reader honest.
When the old site moves to the new platform, plan the content migration early. Redirects and media take the most time.
Measuring the result
Track how long a page takes from idea to live. Shorter cycles show that the workflow fits the team.
